s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant patient with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
Variable first heart sound on auscultation
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
Palpitations lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Normal laboratory tests, including complete blood cell count, kidney function, liver function, thyroid function, serum electrolytes, and cardiac troponin
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG showed regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min
ECG showed regular P waves with varying PR intervals

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia with regular P waves and varying PR intervals

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of regular P waves marching onto QRS complexes

shortlist.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

shortlist.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible presence of an accessory pathway given the regular narrow QRS tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic palpitations, regular narrow QRS tachycardia on ECG, and regular P waves with varying PR intervals are consistent with Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT). The absence of structural heart disease on echocardiography and normal laboratory tests also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: While possible, the varying PR intervals on ECG are not typical for AVNRT, which usually has a more fixed PR interval.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: This diagnosis would typically involve an accessory electrical pathway, which is not clearly indicated by the provided ECG or echocardiography findings.

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition involves an accessory pathway and typically presents with a wide QRS complex if the pathway is used for anterograde conduction, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is characterized by the presence of a delta wave on the ECG, which is not mentioned in the provided ECG findings.

gold: Accelerated atrioventricular junctional tachycardia with isorhythmic atrioventricular dissociation
